reason: Counterexample to "the modulus condition alone implies quasiconformality": conjugation is an orientation-reversing Euclidean isometry, so it preserves every path family's extremal length and satisfies the two-sided modulus inequalities with K=1, yet f_z=0, f_zbar=1 violate |f_zbar| <= k|f_z| for every k<1 and the orientation clause of the geometric definition fails, so f is not 1-quasiconformal in either sense.
